families.name: Eligibility, line integrity and data quality
families.purpose: Pass/fail gates and data checks on the exact LSE line: domicile and the physical-ETC branch, USD quote, product complexity, asset class, freshness, price integrity, proxy mapping and splice, IBKR orderability, coverage and source reconciliation. Gates decide what may receive money and are never averaged into a score. The core's designated line is never blocked by an owner-input or coverage gate.

families.name: Implementation cost on the UCITS line
families.purpose: Line view (the line score sums to 100 within each sleeve). Known-sign drags on the line actually bought, compared like for like with the other lines in the same sleeve: TER, tracking difference beyond TER relative to the same-index reference line, its stability, price noise, traded value, whole-share residue and, later, realised fills. CST10 (15-year all-in cost, including half of the tax-rule-dependent saving) picks the line inside each sleeve.

families.name: Withholding, tax-rule fragility and distribution drag
families.purpose: Line view. Look-through US withholding, used only where 3 or more years of tracking difference are missing; the fragility of a cost advantage that rests on one tax rule; and distribution friction. Pillars with hand-kept, unverified rule tables are recorded, not scored.

families.name: Fund durability and switch readiness
families.purpose: Line view. The chance the line survives 15 years without a forced switch: size, age and ready substitutes are scored. Physical-ETC custody, flows, issuer record, counterparty exposure and benchmark history are recorded or used as gates until their sources are verified. Feeds the structural sell rules.

families.name: Long-horizon expected return
families.purpose: Exposure view (X sums to 100, VWRA = 50, scored on each sleeve's reference index and never on its best line). Only pillars REC04 can rebuild point-in-time are scored: currency value, currency carry and long-term reversal; bond and gold sleeves use their own pillars. CAPE, multi-ratio valuation, payout yield, capital-market assumptions, index drag and country risk premium are recorded until REC03 promotes them. EXR02 turns the scored pillars into an expected return in % a year for FIT04.

families.name: Rewarded factor exposure
families.purpose: Exposure view. Value, profitability, investment and quality-conditioned size loadings from Ken French regional regressions on expanding or rolling windows with a release lag, shrunk by their t-statistics. Beta and alpha are context only. EXR08 and FAC01 together are capped at 25% of X, so value is not counted several times.

families.name: Holdability (one-sided or scale-free against the world)
families.purpose: Exposure view. Penalises crash, recovery and tail risk beyond what the world and beta imply, never rewarding calm. Also holds the portfolio drawdown budget and risk-contribution constraints (weight 0), and the drawdown-protocol and regret display (context).

families.name: Fund-level exposure hazards
families.purpose: Exposure view. Only the specialised-fund hype penalty is scored. Breadth is recorded (no history). Restricted-market exposure is a gate only (above 5% blocks deposits), so the hazard is counted once. Country, currency and sector mix are context; their limits sit in FIT as constraints.

families.name: Fit with the current portfolio (state-dependent)
families.purpose: Fit view, its own 100 points, current portfolio = 50. Expected alpha in % against the current portfolio (40%), down-market correlation, diversification return and ex-ante tracking error against VWRA are scored. Sleeve gap and months-to-cure drive routing and sells. Overlap is context. The US, sector, single-name and line-count limits are hard constraints with weight 0, so one purchase is not penalised five times. Until owner positions exist, the portfolio is taken as 100% core.

families.name: Trend (record only)
families.purpose: 12-1 and residual momentum are recorded and tested in REC04 as a pre-registered variant. A 3-12 month signal cannot survive quarterly targets with two-quarter confirmation, and this system's own momentum test (S3) failed the gate. The crash state, core trend flag and relative-performance display are information only. Trend is never a reason to sell.

families.name: News and structural events (agents)
families.purpose: Ten agents with cited, dated sources. Line events (EVT01, EVT02, EVT05) are penalty-only in the line score and gate deposits at severity 2 or more. Exposure events (EVT03, EVT04, EVT07) carry no weight in X because they cannot be backtested. EVT07 severity 3 is a hard gate, EVT03 only records, and EVT10 numbers are accepted only after code confirms the quoted text. Sentiment is never scored.

families.name: Live record and rule testing
families.purpose: Judges the system on the owner's money and decides when anything may start moving money. Covers money-weighted return against a VWRA-only shadow, point-in-time snapshots of every pillar, live information coefficient by exposure, the exact-rule backtest gate (REC04), the funding and execution log, behaviour and attribution, and the owner policy-mix test (REC07).

families.name: Macro context
families.purpose: Context for the weekly note, the drawdown protocol, order-time caution and the owner's decision on the diversifier share D. Weight 0 because macro predictors fail out of sample (Welch and Goyal 2008). Logged at every deposit (REC02).

pillars.name: Irish or Luxembourg UCITS domicile, non-US-situs, with a physical-ETC branch (gate)
pillars.definition: Pass branch (a): the ISIN starts with IE or LU, the fund is UCITS, and it is not US-situs (IE is preferred over LU on the same index; the cost shows in TAX01). Pass branch (b), for the gold or silver sleeve only: an IE-issued, physically backed precious-metal ETC holding allocated, segregated LBMA bullion in a non-US vault, with a named custodian, confirmed by DUR02. Branch (b) is not UCITS and is eligible for nothing else (ELG04). US-domiciled or US-listed funds fail and can be watched but never bought. A held line turning from pass to fail triggers sell rule S1.
pillars.data_source: universe_ucits_*.csv ISIN and scope columns; iShares UK product page domicile and UCITS fields; DUR02 for branch (b)
pillars.evidence: GOAL.md: US-listed funds cost 30% dividend withholding and carry US estate-tax exposure above US$60,000 (IRC 2101-2106). The Ireland-US treaty gives Irish funds 15%. IGLN.L (IE00B4ND3602) and SGLD.L (IE00B579F325) are Irish-issued ETC notes, not UCITS funds; without branch (b), ELG01 and ELG04 contradicted each other.

pillars.name: USD LSE line and price-unit check (gate)
pillars.definition: Pass if the line trades on the LSE in USD (yfinance currency == USD). A fund held through a GBp, GBP or EUR line is mapped to its USD sibling by ISIN (SSAC.L to ISAC.L, SPXP.L to SPXS.L). A non-USD line is eligible only if its sleeve has no affordable eligible USD line, and its FX cost is then charged in CST10. Flags 100x jumps between GBp and GBP prices.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L currency; universe_ucits_*.csv currency and ISIN columns (GBX, GBp and GBP spellings unified)
pillars.evidence: Probes on 2026-11-07: SPXS.L closes at US$14.95 (USD, 60-day median volume 1.6m shares), while SPXP.L closes at 1118.6 GBp, the same fund's GBP line. The US$1,140 figure in one design was a GBp price read as USD. Naive GBp-vs-USD comparisons produced fake 3-year gaps of 292-342 bps.

pillars.name: Product-complexity gate
pillars.definition: Fails leveraged, inverse, daily-reset, option-overlay (covered-call, buffer) and single-stock products, identified from fund name, universe scope and issuer structure fields.
pillars.data_source: universe_ucits_*.csv name and scope; iShares structure fields; justETF profile replication field
pillars.evidence: Daily-reset funds decay with volatility over long holds (Cheng and Madhavan 2009). Covered-call overlays give up equity upside (Israelov and Nielsen 2015).

pillars.name: Asset-class and sleeve eligibility (gate)
pillars.definition: Maps each line to one sleeve. Equity UCITS lines go to the core or an equity satellite. Physical gold ETCs that pass ELG01(b) go to the gold sleeve only. Investment-grade government or aggregate bond funds with duration of 5 years or more go to the owner-sized diversifier sleeve only. Money-market, T-bill, 0-1 year, ultra-short, overnight-swap and multi-asset funds always fail. Lines with no pre-registered sleeve (for example XDEW S&P 500 equal weight, R2US, CUSS) are scored weekly but cannot receive deposits.
pillars.data_source: universe_ucits_*.csv scope column (corrected: XDEW is us/equal_weight, with duplicates removed); issuer asset-class and duration fields
pillars.evidence: PILLAR_AUDIT: the old composite correlated -0.77 with 1-year volatility and put 7 T-bill or bond funds in its top 20. This gate keeps cash out by construction.

pillars.name: Feed freshness
pillars.definition: LSE trading days since the last print with volume above 0 on the USD line. More than 5 days: not buyable. More than 7 days on a held line: structural review under S1, confirmed with the issuer or an Investegate notice.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L daily close and volume
pillars.evidence: DECISION_RULES rule 1 treats a core feed stale for more than 7 days as structural. SPYY.L showed about 5% zero-volume sessions.

pillars.name: Price integrity
pillars.definition: Count over 252 sessions of daily .L returns beyond 6 robust sigmas that the sleeve reference line does not match on the same or next day (same sign, at least half the size), plus unit jumps and runs of repeated closes. Any unmatched event suspends the line's price-based pillars until explained.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and reference-line daily closes
pillars.evidence: The audit traced fake readings to a stale Yahoo NAV and unit mix-ups. CNDX.L printed the same close on 2026-11-05 and 2026-11-06.

pillars.name: Proxy mapping, approved equivalents and splice fidelity
pillars.definition: (a) The line's benchmark must equal the history proxy's index or an entry in config/approved_equivalents.csv. That file is versioned, owned by the engine and changed only through CHANGELOG. Each row states its allowed use: price splice, holdings stand-in (CNDX holdings for XNAS and EQQU; CSPX for VUAA and SPXS; ISAC for MSCI ACWI lines only, never for tracking difference), or world reference before VT (Ken French Developed market plus RF before 2008-03, then ACWI to 2008-06, then VT). (b) Splice test: at least 24 months of overlap, monthly correlation of 0.98 or more, and an annualised gap of 50 bps or less. If it fails, nothing from the proxy is used and pillars needing 10 years read missing for that exposure.
pillars.data_source: iShares UK 'Benchmark Index' field; universe fund names; justETF profile pages (fetch verified); yfinance monthly closes; Ken French Developed factors
pillars.evidence: Audit mapping errors: USMV/ACWV to MVOL, VTI to CSPX, IOO to VWRA. Daily UCITS-vs-US-proxy tracking error measured 300-380 bps purely from close-time mismatch. VT starts 2008-06, so the 2007-08 stress window needs a declared world reference.

pillars.name: IBKR orderability
pillars.definition: An owner-confirmed flag in config/portfolio.yaml: orderable: {LINE: {ok: true, checked_on: date}}. Renewed every 100 days and when a line first enters the shortlist; expired or absent = fail, except for the core's designated line, which is seeded as orderable from the owner's existing VWRA holding and is never blocked by this gate. If no line in the target sleeve passes, the deposit routes to the next sleeve, then to the core chain VWRA, then FWRA, then ACWD.
pillars.data_source: Owner check in TWS or the IBKR client portal, stored in config/portfolio.yaml (schema added by this revision)
pillars.evidence: Retail access to UCITS lines depends on the IBKR entity and KID availability, and IBKR has no API reachable from this cloud sandbox. Data test 1: portfolio.yaml had no field for it, so as written every line, VWRA included, failed on day one.

pillars.name: Coverage and source freshness
pillars.definition: Share of the line's scored pillar weight, counting only pillars with verified sources, that has a live reading this week. Age limits: holdings 35 days (45 days for issuers that publish month-end, such as Vanguard), tracking difference 100 days, TER 120 days. Below 70% the line cannot receive money, except the core's designated line, which is exempt. Coverage is shown next to every score.
pillars.data_source: Engine pillar table and 'as of' dates
pillars.evidence: PILLAR_AUDIT: missing values filled with 50 hid 14-23% gaps. The Vanguard holdings page is month-end only and was 38 days old on the test date, so a 35-day limit would block VWRA itself.

pillars.name: Cross-source reconciliation
pillars.definition: Compares issuer, Yahoo and justETF-profile figures for TER (2 bps tolerance), fund AUM (10%) and date-matched NAV (20 bps), and look-through region weights against the benchmark (2 points). A breach blocks the affected pillar until resolved and logs which source was used.
pillars.data_source: iShares UK product pages and holdings CSV; justETF profile pages (fetch verified); yfinance .L info; universe_ucits_*.csv
pillars.evidence: Found: universe VWRA TER 0.19% against 0.14% on justETF and in DECISION_RULES (to be corrected in the universe file before launch); XDEW TER listed as 0.20 and 0.15; Yahoo SPYY.L total assets of US$9m; Yahoo VWRA navPrice implying a false 82 bp premium.

pillars.name: TER of the share class
pillars.definition: Ongoing charge of the exact USD share class in bps a year, scored against the sleeve's median eligible line with k = 10 bps. Any rise opens a review (EVT02, S2).
pillars.data_source: iShares UK product page TER; justETF profile TER (fetch verified, e.g. VWRA 0.14%); issuer KIDs confirmed by EVT02; reconciled by ELG10
pillars.evidence: Fees are the one certain drag (Sharpe 1991) and the most reliable predictor of fund outcomes (Kinnel 2016). A 0.15 point gap compounds to about 2.2% of terminal wealth over 15 years.

pillars.name: Tracking difference beyond TER, relative to the sleeve reference line
pillars.definition: For every line: the annualised gap between its USD LSE total return and the same-index sleeve reference line's, over at least 3 years (5 where available), plus the TER difference, shrunk toward 0 by its standard error. Endpoint premium noise is reduced by using 20-day average prices at both ends. This works for every issuer because only LSE closes are needed. Where the reference is an iShares line, the absolute tracking difference against the net index is shown too. Lines on a different index are never compared, so VWRA is never compared with ISAC.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L daily closes (verified for all issuers); iShares UK performance tables for absolute tracking difference
pillars.evidence: Tracking difference persists by fund (Elton, Gruber, Comer and Li 2002). Measured on 2026-11-07, 3 years of LSE closes: SPXS vs CSPX +19.3 bps a year, VUAA vs CSPX -0.1, XNAS vs CNDX +16.8, EQQU vs CNDX +4.2, FWRA vs VWRA +20.4, ACWD vs ISAC +19.8. CSPX beat its net benchmark by about 17 bps a year over 5 years.

pillars.name: Tracking-difference stability
pillars.definition: Standard deviation of the last 5 calendar-year gaps against the sleeve reference line (iShares lines: calendar-year tracking difference from the issuer table), in bps, with k = 15 bps.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L closes; iShares UK calendar-year performance table
pillars.evidence: An erratic yearly gap signals sampling, lending swings or one-off reclaims that may not repeat. A stable gap makes CST02 a better forecast.

pillars.name: Price noise against the sleeve reference line
pillars.definition: Annualised standard deviation of daily return differences against the sleeve reference line over 1 year, in bps.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L daily closes
pillars.evidence: Measured: CSPX vs VUAA 68 bps, CSPX vs SPXS 72 bps, VWRA vs FWRA 218 bps. Higher noise means a larger random premium paid on each buy (Frino and Gallagher 2001).

pillars.name: Quoted bid-ask spread (record until verified)
pillars.definition: A separate weekday job takes one snapshot at 14:00 London, Tuesday to Thursday. A quote is kept only if regularMarketTime is within 25 minutes, bid < ask, both sizes are above 0, and the spread is under 200 bps. The pillar is the 20-snapshot median in bps. Recorded with weight 0 until 20 valid snapshots exist; until then its weight goes to CST06, and CST09 replaces it after 3 owner fills.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L bid, ask and regularMarketTime
pillars.evidence: Data test 2: weekend quotes were stale or crossed (CSPX bid 841.29 above ask 799.20), and Yahoo LSE quotes are delayed about 15 minutes. The Abdi-Ranaldo estimator gave VWRA 0 bps.

pillars.name: LSE traded value and zero-volume days
pillars.definition: Log of the 63-session median daily traded value on the USD line (close x volume, US$), saturating at US$5m a day, minus a penalty for the share of zero-volume sessions (0% none, 20% or more maximum).
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L daily volume and close
pillars.evidence: Liquidity goes with tighter spreads and smaller premiums (Petajisto 2017). Measured medians: CSPX about US$107-158m a day, VWRA about US$40m, FWRA about US$3.6m, SPYY about US$900. Above a few million a day a US$679 order gains nothing.

pillars.name: Premium or discount to NAV (record until verified across issuers)
pillars.definition: Mean |LSE close / issuer NAV - 1| over 20 sessions, matched on NAV date, in bps. Computed for iShares lines from the daily product-page NAV. Recorded with weight 0 because the practical buy lines (VWRA, VUAA, SPXS, XNAS) have no verified NAV source. Yahoo navPrice is never used.
pillars.data_source: iShares UK product page NAV (verified); other issuers' NAV files (unverified)
pillars.evidence: Premiums persist in thinner and international funds (Petajisto 2017) and blew out in March 2020 (Haddad, Moreira and Muir 2021). Yahoo's stale VWRA navPrice implied a false 82 bp premium.

pillars.name: Whole-share residue at deposit size
pillars.definition: Expected uninvested share of an order for whole shares, averaged over orders of US$340-760: (order - commission - floor((order - commission) / price) x price) / order. A line priced above 0.9 x US$679 is flagged as not buyable in one month. Fractional shares are assumed unavailable until EVT08 confirms otherwise.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L USD price; deposit size from config/portfolio.yaml
pillars.evidence: Prices on 2026-11-07: CSPX US$802.21 and CNDX US$1,562.80, both above one deposit; SPXS US$14.95, XNAS US$63.16, VUAA US$143.90, EQQU US$665.13, EXUS US$44.75, EIMI US$48.91. Idle cash forgoes the equity premium.

pillars.name: Realised execution cost from owner fills
pillars.definition: Median over the line's last 6 owner fills of (fill - mid at order entry) / mid plus commission / order, in bps. Missing below 3 fills; from 3 fills it takes 0.10 of CST weight from CST06.
pillars.data_source: IBKR activity statement CSV dropped into inputs/ibkr/ and parsed by the engine; mid at entry from the fills block in config/portfolio.yaml
pillars.evidence: Measures the owner's real order type, size and time, where free estimators fail (CST05). Data test 3: no statement or upload location existed yet.

pillars.name: 15-year all-in cost per deposited dollar (line choice)
pillars.definition: Expected annual cost in bps: minus the CST02 relative tracking difference, plus 0.5 x TAX03 (half the saving that depends on one tax rule, the same logic as sell rule S2), plus one-off entry costs spread over 15 years (commission share, half the spread where CST05 or CST09 exist, and CST08 residue drag at 0.4% a month of forgone return), plus FX cost for a non-USD line. If any candidate in the sleeve lacks CST02, every candidate uses TER + TAX01 instead, so the comparison stays like for like. Weight 0; it ranks lines inside a sleeve.
pillars.data_source: Derived from CST01-CST09, TAX01, TAX03; IBKR commission US$1.70 minimum and FX US$2 minimum in config/portfolio.yaml
pillars.evidence: Holding cost dominates entry cost for a 15-year buyer. Worked figures: SPXS about -26.5 bps (-36 tracking, +9.7 tax-rule haircut) against VUAA about -17 bps, so SPXS is cheaper by about 9.5 bps a year after the haircut. The old version ignored TAX03 in line choice but used it in S2.

pillars.name: US dividend withholding drag
pillars.definition: Look-through US weight x US dividend yield x fund-level rate (Irish physical 15%, Irish swap on a qualified index about 0%, Luxembourg physical 30%), in bps a year. Scored in the line view only when the line has less than 3 years of CST02; otherwise context, because CST02 already contains it.
pillars.data_source: iShares holdings CSV Location column (latest-holdings.csv by productId); vanguard.co.uk month-end region weights for Vanguard lines; US yield from trailing-12-month Ticker.dividends of the US proxy
pillars.evidence: Ireland-US treaty rate 15%. A yield of about 1.3% x 15% is about 20 bps, which matches the measured 19 bps SPXS-over-CSPX gap. Data test 4 verified the holdings URL pattern and the ttm-dividend method.

pillars.name: Non-US level-1 withholding drag (record)
pillars.definition: Sum over countries of fund weight x country dividend yield x unrecoverable rate for an Irish or Luxembourg fund, in bps a year. Recorded with weight 0 until the treaty table is verified; CST02 captures the realised effect meanwhile.
pillars.data_source: Holdings Location weights (verified); country ttm yields from EWJ, EWU, EWG, MCHI and INDA Ticker.dividends (verified; INDA flagged, no dividend in 23 months); treaty-rate table maintained by hand (unverified)
pillars.evidence: Gross-to-net index gaps show 10-30 bps for ex-US and EM. The hand-kept table has no verified source, so it cannot move money.

pillars.name: Tax-rule dependence of a cost advantage
pillars.definition: Part of the line's all-in cost advantage over its physical same-index peer that depends on one tax rule (for example the section 871(m) qualified-index exemption for swap S&P 500 lines), in bps. One-sided: 0 bps scores 50, falling to the floor at 25 bps or more. Half of it is charged in CST10.
pillars.data_source: Derived from replication type (justETF profile, verified: SPXS 'Synthetic (Unfunded swap)') and CST02; rule status watched by EVT06
pillars.evidence: The measured swap advantage (19.3 bps a year, SPXS vs CSPX) would disappear if the rule changes. Pricing that fragility keeps new-money line choice and the S2 switch rule consistent.

pillars.name: Bond-interest withholding (diversifier sleeve, record)
pillars.definition: Share of a bond fund's income not exempt for an Irish fund x rate x yield, in bps a year. Recorded with weight 0 until the rules table is verified.
pillars.data_source: iShares UK bond holdings CSV Location column (verified); rules table maintained by hand (unverified)
pillars.evidence: The US portfolio-interest exemption (IRC 871(h), 881(c)) frees most US bond interest. The old G09 wrongly applied 30% to bond yields.

pillars.name: Distribution friction
pillars.definition: 0 for an accumulating class. For a distributing class (for example EQQU): the cost of reinvesting each payment (US$1.70 / payment) or its cash drag, in bps a year. A distributing class is eligible only where its sleeve has no affordable accumulating USD line.
pillars.data_source: universe_ucits_*.csv accumulating column; yield from the proxy's ttm dividends
pillars.evidence: Irish funds pay non-residents without Irish withholding and the UAE has no income tax, so only the reinvestment commission and idle cash differ.

pillars.name: Fund and share-class size (merged)
pillars.definition: min(fund AUM, 5 x share-class AUM) where the share-class AUM is known, otherwise fund AUM, in US$, log-scaled from US$50m and saturating at US$5bn.
pillars.data_source: iShares UK 'Net Assets of Fund' and 'of Share Class'; justETF profile fund size (fetch verified, e.g. VWRA EUR 56.3bn); yfinance totalAssets (e.g. VUAA US$89.0bn, EXUS US$8.2bn); reconciled by ELG10
pillars.evidence: European ETF closures concentrate in funds under about US$100m. The old DUR01 and DUR02 were identical for single-class funds such as CSPX and were merged.

pillars.name: Physical-ETC structure and custody (gold sleeve gate)
pillars.definition: For ELG01 branch (b): the metal is allocated and segregated, LBMA good-delivery, held by a named custodian in a vault outside the US, with an independent trustee or security over the metal, and no unsecured counterparty beyond settlement. Pass or fail, confirmed from the product page or base prospectus, or by an owner check with a date in config/portfolio.yaml. Re-checked yearly and on any EVT05 custodian event. Weight 0 (gate).
pillars.data_source: iShares Physical Gold ETC product page and base prospectus PDF; Invesco pages (HTTP 406, blocked); owner check
pillars.evidence: An ETC is a debt note of a special-purpose issuer: holders rely on the allocated metal and the security arrangement, not on UCITS diversification rules. Without this check the gold sleeve had no valid gate.

pillars.name: Net flows, 12 months (one-sided, record until history exists)
pillars.definition: (Shares outstanding now - 12 months ago) x NAV / AUM 12 months ago, in %. Outflows penalised, inflows neutral. Missing until 52 weekly snapshots exist (from 2027-W45); the signed series is logged for REC03.
pillars.data_source: iShares UK shares outstanding snapshotted weekly from 2026-W45; for others, justETF size change minus price return (unverified)
pillars.better_when: higher up to 0 (outflows bad, inflows neutral)
pillars.evidence: Outflows come before closures. Inflows are not rewarded because flows chase returns (Dannhauser and Pontiff 2019; Ben-David et al. 2023). The series only began this month.

pillars.name: Share-class age
pillars.definition: Years since the USD line launched, saturating at 5. The universe or issuer first date is preferred over yfinance fundInceptionDate.
pillars.data_source: universe_ucits_*.csv first_date; iShares inception date; justETF profile inception
pillars.evidence: Closure risk is highest in the first 3 years. yfinance gave XNAS a 2026-09 inception against the true 2021-01-21, hence the source order.

pillars.name: Issuer scale and closure record (record)
pillars.definition: Mean of the issuer's European ETF AUM (log) and its UCITS closures and mergers over 5 years per average line count. Weight 0 until a closure list is verified.
pillars.data_source: justETF closure lists (404); issuer annual reports; Investegate notices
pillars.evidence: Small issuers prune ranges more often, but data test 6 found no working closed-fund list.

pillars.name: Switch-ready substitutes
pillars.definition: Number of other eligible LSE USD lines on the same or an approved equivalent index with TER within 0.10% and CST02 within 0.15% of this line; a different issuer counts double. 0 scores worst, 2 or more saturates.
pillars.data_source: universe_ucits_*.csv (with EXUS, ACWD and SPYY added, EQAC removed) with gates applied; CST01, CST02
pillars.evidence: Substitutes: VWRA has FWRA (and ACWD and SPYY on MSCI ACWI as approved equivalents); S&P 500 lines have each other; XNAS has CNDX and EQQU. EQAC.L returned 404 on yfinance and is not in the universe. The ex-US sleeve has only EXUS, so it has no substitute.

pillars.name: Counterparty and lending exposure (record)
pillars.definition: Physical fund: average % of NAV on loan over 1 year (iShares disclosure). Swap fund: replication and counterparties from the justETF profile as a flag; net swap exposure % when available. Weight 0 until swap exposure percentages are verified.
pillars.data_source: iShares UK lending table (verified); justETF profile counterparties (fetch verified); Invesco pages 406; Xtrackers JS app
pillars.evidence: UCITS caps counterparty exposure at 10% of NAV with collateral, so the risk sits in the tail. Data test 7: swap exposure percentages could not be fetched.

pillars.name: Benchmark-change history (record)
pillars.definition: Number of benchmark or provider changes, built from the engine's weekly snapshots of the benchmark field from now on, plus 1 for a pending consultation flagged by EVT04. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: Engine weekly snapshots; EVT04 output; current KID only (no history available)
pillars.evidence: Issuers switch indices to cut licence fees (Vanguard 2012, MSCI to FTSE and CRSP). Data test 8: issuers publish only the latest KID.

pillars.name: CAPE yield and CAPE against own history (record)
pillars.definition: Records US 1/CAPE and the US CAPE z-score against its 20-year history weekly. Regional look-through 1/CAPE is recorded once config/cape.csv rows pass EVT10's code check. Weight 0, and missing for every exposure in scoring, including the US and VWRA, so data-rich exposures are not handicapped against data-poor ones.
pillars.data_source: Shiller ie_data.xls scraped each run from the shillerdata.com link (verified to 2026.10, CAPE 40.71; dates read as strings), never the stale Yale URL; regional CAPE (unverified: Research Affiliates JS app, Barclays login)
pillars.evidence: CAPE predicts 10-15 year returns (Campbell and Shiller 1998; Keimling 2016), but its 10-year R2 comes from overlapping windows (Boudoukh, Richardson and Whitelaw 2008). VWRA's own look-through CAPE cannot be computed without non-US CAPE.

pillars.name: Expected excess return in % a year (FIT04 input)
pillars.data_source: EXR06-EXR08, FAC01-FAC04, EXR10, CST10 (all verified); FRED DTB3
pillars.evidence: Audit blocker: FIT04 took E[R] from a 0-100 score with no unit mapping. A building-block return with pre-registered coefficients (Grinold and Kroner 2002; Black-Litterman-style shrinkage toward the market) is deterministic. ERP_world is set near the Dimson-Marsh-Staunton long-run world premium over bills. Withholding enters once, through CST10's tracking difference, not through EXR04.

pillars.name: Multi-ratio valuation yield (record)
pillars.definition: Mean robust z-score, against VWRA, of holdings' E/P, B/P, CF/P and S/P. yfinance returns these as yields even under P/E labels, and that is documented. Weight 0, recorded from now on (no history, so REC04 cannot test it).
pillars.data_source: yfinance funds_data equity_holdings (verified, e.g. VWRA.L 'Price/Earnings' 0.0489 = 4.89% E/P); iShares P/E and P/B fields
pillars.evidence: Value predicts across countries (Asness, Liew and Stevens 1997; Asness, Moskowitz and Pedersen 2013), but the cheap regions trailed VT in both 2015-19 and 2020-26 (EEM 5.8%, EFA 7.5% vs VT 10.6% a year). Untested, it is not allowed to move money.

pillars.name: Dividend yield after withholding (record)
pillars.definition: Trailing-12-month dividends of the same-index US proxy (accumulating UCITS lines report 0) / price, after fund-level withholding, in %. The buyback leg is dropped. INDA is flagged (no dividend in 23 months). Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: yfinance Ticker.dividends of the proxy (verified, e.g. VT 1.56%); TAX01
pillars.evidence: Payout yield predicts returns (Boudoukh et al. 2007), but data test 11 showed S&P DJI buyback data returns 403 and accumulating lines report 0 yield.

pillars.name: CMA consensus 10-year return (record)
pillars.definition: Mean 10-year nominal USD expected return across at least 3 houses, shrunk toward VWRA's by 1 / (1 + range / 2 points). Rows in config/cma.csv must carry house, exposure, horizon, nominal_usd, url, quoted_text and published_on. Code fetches the URL and confirms the number before use, and rejects rows older than 200 days. Weight 0; recorded, and used only as a cross-check on EXR02.
pillars.data_source: config/cma.csv (schema defined here; file not yet created), filled by EVT10
pillars.evidence: Combining forecasts reduces error (Clemen 1989), but house CMAs are largely CAPE-built, so scoring them would count value again. Data test 12: the file does not exist.

pillars.name: Currency valuation
pillars.definition: Exposure-weighted z-score of each non-USD currency's BIS real effective exchange rate against its 20-year mean, inverted so cheaper scores higher; computed point-in-time on expanding data with FRED release lags. USD-only exposures score 0, relative to VWRA's non-USD share. In X.
pillars.data_source: FRED BIS REER series (RBXMBIS, RBJPBIS, RBGBBIS, RBCNBIS, RBINBIS, RBUSBIS); holdings currency weights
pillars.evidence: Real exchange rates revert with a 3-5 year half-life (Rogoff 1996), and currency value predicts currency returns (Menkhoff et al. 2017). This matters for an unhedged owner whose AED is pegged to the USD.

pillars.name: Currency carry
pillars.definition: Sum over non-USD currencies of unhedged weight x (local 3-month rate - US 3-month rate), in %, point-in-time. A currency with no current rate is dropped for every exposure, VWRA included. In X at low weight.
pillars.data_source: FRED OECD 3-month rates and DTB3 (verified; GBP ends 2026-01, so GBP is dropped symmetrically until a Bank of England series is verified); Bank of Canada Valet for CAD
pillars.evidence: Carry earns a premium (Lustig, Roussanov and Verdelhan 2011; Koijen et al. 2018) but crashes in risk-off episodes (Brunnermeier, Nagel and Pedersen 2008).

pillars.name: Long-term reversal
pillars.definition: USD total return of the sleeve's reference index (spliced under ELG07) from month -60 to month -13, minus VWRA's over the same window. Price-only, so it is rebuilt exactly in REC04. Together with FAC01 it is capped at 25% of X.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy adjusted closes
pillars.evidence: Country indices mean-revert over 3-5 years (Richards 1997; Balvers, Wu and Gilliland 2000), and this is the price-based value proxy (Asness, Moskowitz and Pedersen 2013). It replaces the wrong-signed CAGR pillars (De Bondt and Thaler 1985). Its correlation with FAC01 is checked before launch (REC03).

pillars.name: Index construction drag (record)
pillars.definition: Index one-way turnover x asset-class trading cost, plus a front-running estimate for indices with predictable additions, in bps a year. Turnover comes from 12 months of iShares monthly holdings snapshots. Weight 0 until turnover exists for every sleeve's index.
pillars.data_source: iShares holdings snapshots (building from 2026-11); Petajisto (2011) parameters; yfinance annualHoldingsTurnover returned None for VWRA.L
pillars.evidence: Index-change costs are about 21-28 bps a year for the S&P 500 and 38-77 bps for the Russell 2000 (Petajisto 2011). The earlier claim that VWRA turnover of 7% was verified was wrong (data probe).

pillars.name: Bond expected return (diversifier sleeve only)
pillars.definition: Yield to worst minus expected default loss by rating (AAA-A 0.05%, BBB 0.2%, BB 1%, B and below 3%, x 0.6), minus TER, plus Treasury roll-down at the fund's duration, plus hedge carry for a hedged class, in %. Replaces the equity pillars for bond lines.
pillars.data_source: iShares UK bond product pages and holdings CSV (verified, e.g. AGGU); FRED DGS1-DGS30
pillars.evidence: Starting yield explains most of a bond fund's 5-10 year return (Leibowitz, Bova and Kogelman 2014).

pillars.name: Gold real-price valuation (gold sleeve, record until history verified)
pillars.definition: Percentile of the USD gold price deflated by US CPI within its history from 1975 to today. Missing until a 1975+ gold series is verified, because a percentile inside 2000+ only is uninformative. Then it feeds EXR02's gold mapping.
pillars.data_source: yfinance GC=F (from 2000-08 only); FRED LBMA series removed (HTML); candidate World Bank Pink Sheet monthly gold (untested); FRED CPIAUCSL
pillars.evidence: A high real gold price has been followed by low real returns (Erb and Harvey 2013). Data auditor: GC=F starts 2000-08, so the 1975 window was unsourced.

pillars.name: Country risk premium (test only)
pillars.definition: Look-through weighted Damodaran country risk premium, in %. Weight 0 until REC03 promotes it.
pillars.data_source: Damodaran ctryprem.xlsx (download verified)
pillars.evidence: Country ratings explain returns in sample (Erb, Harvey and Viskanta 1996), but out-of-sample evidence is weak.

pillars.name: Value loading
pillars.definition: HML beta from a 60-month regression of the reference index's USD excess returns on the matching regional Ken French 5 factors plus momentum (Newey-West), estimated each month with only data released by then (1-month lag), shrunk by min(1, |t| / 2). Shares a 25% cap of X with EXR08.
pillars.data_source: Ken French data library, US, Developed and Emerging files (verified); yfinance monthly returns
pillars.evidence: Fama and French (1992, 1998, 2015). The premium was weak from about 2007 to 2020 (Fama and French 2021), so the weight is small and capped with EXR08.

pillars.name: Profitability loading
pillars.definition: RMW beta from the same point-in-time regression, shrunk by min(1, |t| / 2).
pillars.data_source: Ken French data library; yfinance
pillars.evidence: Novy-Marx (2013); Fama and French (2015, 2017); Asness, Frazzini and Pedersen (2019). Robust across regions.

pillars.name: Investment loading
pillars.definition: CMA beta from the same point-in-time regression, shrunk by min(1, |t| / 2).
pillars.data_source: Ken French data library; yfinance
pillars.evidence: Fama and French (2015); Hou, Xue and Zhang (2015).

pillars.name: Size loading, conditional on quality
pillars.definition: SMB beta counts only if the RMW beta is 0 or above; otherwise 0.
pillars.data_source: Ken French data library; yfinance
pillars.evidence: The plain size premium is weak (Alquist, Israel and Moskowitz 2018) but appears once junk is controlled for (Asness et al. 2018).

pillars.name: Market beta and residual alpha (context)
pillars.definition: World-market beta and the annualised intercept with t-statistic from the same regression. Weight 0. Beta feeds RSK01, RSK04, FIT04 and FIT10.
pillars.data_source: Ken French data library; yfinance
pillars.evidence: Rewarding low beta would favour defensive and cash-like funds (Frazzini and Pedersen 2014 is about leverage within an asset class). Past alpha does not persist (Carhart 1997).

pillars.name: Excess drawdown beyond beta
pillars.definition: Maximum drawdown of the reference index over an expanding window, at least 10 years and spliced under ELG07, monthly USD, minus beta x the world's drawdown over the same window. One-sided, k = 10 points: VWRA and anything calmer score 50.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy monthly returns; world reference per ELG07
pillars.evidence: Nasdaq-100 fell about 80% in 2000-02 against about 50% for the world. The one-sided form gives no credit for calm.

pillars.name: Excess time under water
pillars.definition: Longest peak-to-recovery spell in months minus the world's over the same expanding window; an unrecovered drawdown counts to date. One-sided, k = 24 months.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy monthly returns
pillars.evidence: Japan took about 34 years and Nasdaq-100 about 15 years to regain their peaks. Long recoveries make owners abandon a plan.

pillars.name: Downside-upside beta asymmetry
pillars.definition: Beta to the world in down months minus beta in up months over 10 years, point-in-time. Scale-free.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy monthly returns
pillars.evidence: Downside beta is priced (Ang, Chen and Xing 2006), and correlations rise in falling markets (Longin and Solnik 2001).

pillars.name: Stress-window shortfall, beta-adjusted
pillars.definition: Mean of (exposure return - beta x world return) over Oct 2007-Mar 2009, Feb-Mar 2020 and calendar 2022. The world reference before VT follows ELG07 (Ken French Developed market plus RF, then ACWI from 2008-03). Only shortfalls count (one-sided, k = 5 points); missing windows are excluded for every exposure.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy history; Ken French Developed factors
pillars.evidence: Three crisis types reveal regime-specific fragility. VT starts 2008-06, so the 2007 start needed a declared reference.

pillars.name: Tail fatness
pillars.definition: Monthly 95% CVaR divided by monthly volatility over 10 years. Scale-free. Half the internal weight of RSK01-RSK04.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy monthly returns
pillars.evidence: Tail risk beyond the normal is a holdability hazard (Kelly and Jiang 2014). Negative coskewness may be priced (Harvey and Siddique 2000), hence the half weight. This was RSK06; the old RSK05 regret pillar is now display only (RSK08).

pillars.name: Portfolio drawdown budget (constraint)
pillars.definition: Replays the proposed target mix (owner policy or score targets) through 2008-09, 2011, 2020 Q1 and 2022, monthly and spliced. Worst loss minus the world's worst must be 5 points or less. Tilts are scaled down until it holds. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy monthly returns; target mix
pillars.evidence: GOAL success measure: worst drawdown against the world market.

pillars.name: Risk-contribution ratio (constraint)
pillars.definition: Each sleeve's share of portfolio variance (10-year Ledoit-Wolf monthly covariance) divided by its capital weight; 1.5 or less at target weights. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy monthly returns; target mix
pillars.evidence: Capital weights understate a volatile satellite's risk (Qian 2005; Maillard, Roncalli and Teiletche 2010).

pillars.name: Drawdown protocol, volatility and regret display (context)
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L closes; owner positions (core-only fallback)
pillars.evidence: Investors lose 1-1.7 points a year trading around drawdowns (Morningstar 'Mind the Gap'; Dichev 2007). In-sample regret had the opposite sign to EXR08 and penalised EM and value for past outcomes, so it is shown, not scored.

pillars.name: Breadth of holdings (record)
pillars.definition: Effective number of issuers, 1 / sum of squared look-through issuer weights (share classes merged), log-scaled and saturating at 500. Weight 0 in X because it has no history for REC04; recorded weekly.
pillars.data_source: iShares latest-holdings.csv by productId; vanguard.co.uk month-end holdings; yfinance top holdings; SSGA removed (unverified)
pillars.evidence: About 4% of US stocks created all net wealth (Bessembinder 2018), so breadth matters, but the scored X may only hold point-in-time-testable pillars.

pillars.name: Country and currency mix (context)
pillars.definition: Largest country weight, half the sum of |country weight - world weight|, non-USD share and a hedged flag. Weight 0; portfolio limits sit in FIT07.
pillars.data_source: Holdings Location and Market Currency columns (iShares CSV; Vanguard month-end)
pillars.evidence: Scoring this at fund level would penalise an S&P 500 sleeve twice.

pillars.name: Sector mix and index concentration (context)
pillars.definition: Half the sum of |GICS sector weight - world sector weight|, the top-10 weight, and its percentile in the index's own logged history. Weight 0; portfolio limits sit in FIT08 and FIT09.
pillars.data_source: Holdings Sector column; ISAC as the MSCI ACWI sector reference; weekly snapshots
pillars.evidence: Evidence that concentration predicts returns is mixed, so it is shown as something to watch.

pillars.name: Restricted-market exposure (gate only)
pillars.definition: Look-through weight in markets listed in config/restricted_markets.csv. Every row has a primary-source citation and a date, added by EVT07 and checked by code. Above 5%, the line cannot receive deposits. Weight 0, so the hazard is counted once.
pillars.data_source: Holdings Location column (verified); config/restricted_markets.csv
pillars.evidence: Russia 2022: removal at an effectively zero price and suspended ETFs. Auditors found this hazard counted three times (score, gate and EVT07 penalty).

pillars.name: Specialised or thematic hype penalty
pillars.definition: 1 for a narrow thematic, single-industry or single-frontier-country fund launched within 5 years, or after a top-quintile 36-month index return, or with 12-month inflows above 50% of AUM. 0.5 for other narrow sector or theme funds. 0 for broad funds. Point-in-time from launch dates and index history. In X.
pillars.data_source: universe_ucits_*.csv scope tags and first_date; yfinance index history
pillars.evidence: Specialised ETFs launched into hype underperform by about 6% a year over 5 years (Ben-David, Franzoni, Kim and Moussawi 2023, Review of Financial Studies).

pillars.name: Sleeve gap (routing input)
pillars.definition: For each sleeve: gap = target x (portfolio value + C) - sleeve value, in US$. Weight 0. If positions are missing or older than 35 days, the whole deposit goes to the core.
pillars.data_source: config/portfolio.yaml positions [{line, units, avg_cost_usd, as_of}], later the IBKR statement parser (inputs/ibkr/); yfinance .L prices
pillars.evidence: Rebalancing with new cash keeps the mix on target without selling or timing (Jaconetti, Kinniry and Zilbering 2010). Data test 1: no positions schema existed.

pillars.name: Months to cure drift with deposits
pillars.definition: For each overweight sleeve: (sleeve value - band max x portfolio value) / monthly deposit, plus consecutive month-ends outside its band. Weight 0; used by S3.
pillars.data_source: Engine, from FIT01 history and config/portfolio.yaml positions
pillars.evidence: Separates drift that deposits will fix from a breach only a sale can fix.

pillars.name: Overlap with current holdings (context)
pillars.definition: Sum over securities of min(fund weight, portfolio look-through weight), in %. Weight 0, shown to the owner.
pillars.data_source: iShares holdings CSV; vanguard.co.uk month-end holdings for VWRA and VUAA; ELG07 stand-ins for XNAS and SPXS; portfolio = core if positions are missing
pillars.evidence: A VUAA or SPXS deposit mostly re-buys VWRA's 62% US. Active share does not predict returns (Frazzini, Friedman and Pomorski 2016), so this is context, not a fifth penalty.

pillars.name: Expected alpha against the current portfolio
pillars.definition: alpha_i = E[R_i - R_f] - beta_i,P x E[R_P - R_f], in % a year. E comes from EXR02 and E[R_P - R_f] = sum of w_k x EXR02_k. Beta uses a 10-year Ledoit-Wolf monthly covariance. P is the core alone until positions exist. 40% of FIT. Cash scores 0 by construction. Required above 0 for a score-driven target (only after REC04 passes); shown as a warning on owner policy targets.
pillars.data_source: EXR02; yfinance .L and proxy monthly returns
pillars.evidence: An asset raises the Sharpe ratio when its expected excess return exceeds beta x the portfolio's (Treynor and Black 1973; Elton, Gruber and Padberg 1976). It is now computed in return units, so the qualification test is deterministic.

pillars.name: Down-market correlation with the portfolio
pillars.definition: Correlation of monthly returns with the current portfolio (core if positions are missing) in months when the world fell, over 10 years with at least 20 such months. Equity and gold lines only.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy monthly returns
pillars.evidence: Correlations rise in falling markets (Longin and Solnik 2001). Scale-free, so it does not reward low volatility.

pillars.name: Diversification return
pillars.definition: Change in 0.5 x (sum w_i sigma_i^2 - sigma_p^2), annualised in bps, moving from the current mix to 95% current + 5% this fund (10-year monthly).
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy monthly returns
pillars.evidence: Booth and Fama (1992); Willenbrock (2011). It rewards volatile, low-correlation assets, which offsets any low-volatility bias.

pillars.name: US look-through weight (constraint)
pillars.definition: Portfolio US weight after the order (and at target) minus the world US weight. Hard limit +10 points. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: Holdings Location (iShares CSV; Vanguard month-end; ELG07 stand-ins)
pillars.evidence: VWRA is already about 62% US. FIT03, FIT07, FIT08, FIT09 and FIT10 all rise with the same S&P or Nasdaq weight, so only FIT10 is scored and the others are limits.

pillars.name: Sector deviation and tech share (constraint)
pillars.definition: Information Technology plus Communication Services at no more than world + 10 points, and total sector deviation at no more than 15 points, after the order and at target. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: Holdings Sector column; ISAC sector reference
pillars.evidence: The largest concentrated drawdowns came from sector bubbles (2000-02). Nasdaq-100 is over 50% technology.

pillars.name: Single-name concentration (constraint)
pillars.definition: Largest single-company look-through weight with share classes combined, 7% or less after the order and at target. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: iShares holdings CSV; Vanguard month-end holdings; yfinance top holdings (SSGA removed)
pillars.evidence: Single-name risk is not compensated (Bessembinder 2018). Stacking S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 on VWRA multiplies the same mega-caps.

pillars.name: Ex-ante tracking error against VWRA
pillars.definition: Forecast annual tracking error of the post-order portfolio against VWRA (10-year Ledoit-Wolf), in %. Scored one-sided with no penalty up to 2%; hard limit 3%. The only scored active-risk measure.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy monthly returns
pillars.evidence: The first success measure is money-weighted return against VWRA, so active risk is the budget every tilt spends (Grinold and Kahn).

pillars.name: Line count and duplicate-exposure guard (gate)
pillars.definition: Blocks a candidate whose 3-year weekly correlation with a held line is 0.97 or more on the same index family, unless it is that line's designated replacement under S1 or S2. At most 4 lines in total, counting diversifier lines. Positions under 2% are flagged. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: config/portfolio.yaml positions (core-only fallback); yfinance weekly returns; universe index families
pillars.evidence: GOAL: a few hours a month and one or two funds per buy. Holding VWRA and FWRA adds tickets with no diversification.

pillars.name: 12-1 momentum against VWRA (record)
pillars.definition: USD return from month -12 to -1 of the reference index minus VWRA's. Weight 0; logged by REC02 and tested in REC04 as one pre-registered variant.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy adjusted closes
pillars.evidence: Momentum decayed after publication (McLean and Pontiff 2016), and S3 here lost 4-6% a year in 2015-19. A 3-12 month signal is stale by the time a two-quarter confirmation sets a target.

pillars.name: Residual momentum against the world (record)
pillars.definition: Cumulative residual return over months -12 to -2 from a 36-month regression on world returns. Weight 0; logged and tested as part of the REC04 momentum variant.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy monthly returns
pillars.evidence: Residual momentum has about half the crash risk (Blitz, Huij and Martens 2011), but it inherits MOM01's horizon problem.

pillars.name: Momentum-crash state (context)
pillars.definition: On when the world's 24-month return is below 0 and its 1-month return is above 0. Neutralises the recorded MOM01 and MOM02 values.
pillars.data_source: yfinance VWRA.L spliced with VT
pillars.evidence: Momentum crashes cluster in rebounds after bear markets (Daniel and Moskowitz 2016).

pillars.name: Core trend flag
pillars.definition: VWRA.L month-end close against its 10-month average and the sign of its 12-1 return. Information only.
pillars.data_source: yfinance VWRA.L
pillars.evidence: Selling the core on trend (S8) trailed holding by 1-3 points a year.

pillars.name: Holdings and candidates against VWRA (weekly display)
pillars.definition: Excess USD return over VWRA.L for each holding and each sleeve's reference line over 1, 3 and 12 months, and the 3-year information ratio. Display only; this is the weekly 'how is each holding doing' answer.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L closes
pillars.evidence: Past relative performance persists only weakly (Carhart 1997), so it is shown, not scored.

pillars.name: Money-weighted return against a VWRA-only portfolio
pillars.definition: Since start and rolling 12 months: the actual portfolio's money-weighted return after all costs against a shadow VWRA-only portfolio with identical deposits; also the money-weighted minus time-weighted gap and worst drawdown against the world.
pillars.data_source: IBKR statements in inputs/ibkr/ (parser to build); yfinance VWRA.L
pillars.evidence: GOAL success measure 1.

pillars.name: Point-in-time pick and pillar snapshot
pillars.data_source: Engine plan log (to be created); yfinance .L closes; FRED
pillars.evidence: The live record is the only test of pillars without history. Data test 16: the plan log did not exist yet.

pillars.name: Pre-launch redundancy check and live information coefficient by exposure
pillars.definition: Before week 1: a Spearman matrix of every scored pillar over the 318 unique lines and the sleeve reference indices; any pair with |rho| of 0.85 or more is merged before launch, and EXR08 vs FAC01 must be below 0.7 or FAC01 is set to record-only. Live: rank IC of each family and each record-only pillar against forward 13, 52 and 156-week returns versus VWRA, one row per exposure or index family (never per line), with non-overlapping windows or Newey-West errors. Promotion: IC above 0 with t above 2 after 36 months. Demotion: only after 36 months, never on 13 or 52-week IC for EXR or FAC. The CST family is tested within each sleeve against the same-index peer's forward return gap.
pillars.data_source: Engine score history from 2026-W45; yfinance .L closes
pillars.evidence: Lines on one index (VUAA, CSPX, SPXS) inflate the cross-section, and overlapping windows overstate t-statistics. A 52-week test of a 10-year signal is noise (Davis et al. 2012).

pillars.name: Exact-rule backtest and score-target gate
pillars.data_source: Engine; Ken French; FRED; Shiller; yfinance; runs/backtest_latest.json
pillars.evidence: GOAL evidence rule and DECISION_RULES gate. All four audits flagged that the old REC04 tested a smaller rule than the live one, used US$2,500 deposits and kept N_TRIALS at 8 after the thresholds were tuned on 2015-2026.

pillars.name: Execution and funding log
pillars.definition: For each order: the line's return minus VWRA's between the Friday signal close and the fill; fill minus mid at entry; and the funding cost (bank wire and correspondent fees, the IBKR AED/USD rate against 3.6725, and the FX minimum). Re-checks the batching choice (k months) each quarter.
pillars.data_source: IBKR statements and bank advice in inputs/ibkr/; funding block in config/portfolio.yaml; yfinance .L closes
pillars.better_when: lower cost and no systematic drift
pillars.evidence: S5 flipped sign between execution timings. The US$2 FX minimum is 29 bps of US$680, more than the commission.

pillars.name: Behaviour, sell log and attribution
pillars.definition: Monthly: deposits on schedule, days from deposit to order, every sale with its rule and hold counterfactual, overrides, and a Brinson split of active return against VWRA into owner-policy sleeve choice, score-driven sleeve choice and line choice. Also line regret 12 months after each buy against the best same-index line.
pillars.data_source: IBKR statements; runs/plan_log.csv; yfinance .L closes
pillars.better_when: all deposits on schedule; zero non-structural sells; line regret near or above 0
pillars.evidence: GOAL success measure: no unforced sells. The attribution shows which part adds or loses money.

pillars.name: Owner policy-mix test against VWRA
pillars.data_source: yfinance VT, SPY, QQQ, EFA, EEM monthly (verified); world proxy before VT = 55% SPY, 35% EFA, 10% EEM
pillars.better_when: higher, and positive in every period
pillars.evidence:
Run on 2026-11-07, money-weighted, same-month execution.
- 2015-26: VT 11.69%; VT90/SPY10 11.95%; VT90/QQQ10 12.39%; VT80/SPY10/QQQ10 12.66%; VT85/EEM5/EFA10 11.24%.
- 2008-14: world 10.79% against 12.38% for 80/10/10.
- 2003-07: world 14.94% against 14.07% for 80/10/10.
The US tilt won after 2008 and lost before it: a regime bet, not a proven edge.

pillars.name: Recession indicators
pillars.definition: 10-year minus 3-month spread (level and months inverted in the last 24) and the real-time Sahm rule against 0.5, with false-alarm notes. Context.
pillars.data_source: FRED T10Y3M, SAHMREALTIME
pillars.evidence: They forecast recessions (Estrella and Mishkin 1998; Sahm 2019) but not returns out of sample (Welch and Goyal 2008).

pillars.name: Credit and financial stress
pillars.definition: US high-yield and EM corporate OAS (20-year percentile, 3-month change), the St. Louis Fed stress index, the Chicago NFCI, and EPU and GPR percentiles. Context for the drawdown note.
pillars.data_source: FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2, BAMLEMCBPIOAS, STLFSI4, NFCI; policyuncertainty.com; Caldara-Iacoviello GPR
pillars.evidence: Spreads carry stress information (Gilchrist and Zakrajsek 2012) with no out-of-sample timing value; the old composite never triggered a correct sell (S6).

pillars.name: Volatility regime (execution caution)
pillars.definition: VIX, VIX/VIX3M and MOVE. When VIX is above 30 or VIX/VIX3M is above 1, the order uses a limit at mid and avoids the first and last 30 minutes. Never delays or skips the deposit.
pillars.data_source: yfinance ^VIX, ^VIX3M, ^MOVE
pillars.evidence: Spreads widen when volatility spikes (Chordia, Roll and Subrahmanyam 2001).

pillars.name: Rates, inflation, dollar and stock-bond regime
pillars.definition: 10-year TIPS yield, 5y5y breakeven, US CPI, 12-month broad-dollar change, AED/USD against 3.6725, 36-month equity-bond correlation, and the US excess CAPE yield (Shiller). Context for the owner's decision on the diversifier share D.
pillars.data_source: FRED DFII10, T5YIFR, CPIAUCSL, DTWEXBGS; yfinance AED=X, VT, IEF, AGGU.L; Shiller via shillerdata.com
pillars.evidence: The stock-bond correlation depends on the inflation regime (Ilmanen 2003), and the excess CAPE yield has weak timing power (Asness 2003).

pillars.name: Fund corporate actions
pillars.definition: Agent scans held and shortlisted lines for closure, merger, liquidation, share-class conversion, delisting, ISIN or ticker change, or loss of the USD line. Severity: 0 none, 1 watch, 2 review (confirmed notice), 3 act. Two dated, cited sources are required, and a primary source (issuer notice or an RNS item via Investegate, with daily NAV notices filtered out) for severity 2 or more. Penalty-only in the line score (50, 40, 25, 0). Severity 2 or more blocks deposits and opens S1.
pillars.data_source: Web search; investegate.co.uk RNS pages (verified); issuer notices
pillars.evidence: DECISION_RULES rule 1 structural triggers. Data test 6: LSE RNS returns 403 or needs JavaScript, while Investegate lists VWRA items to 06 Nov 2026.

pillars.name: Fees, structure, KID and cheaper substitutes
pillars.definition: Agent detects TER, replication, lending, distribution-policy and domicile changes and KID availability. It confirms non-iShares TERs monthly from the justETF profile and the issuer KID (feeding CST01 and ELG10). It also reports new LSE USD lines or fee cuts on any sleeve's index. Penalty-only in the line score: an adverse confirmed change is severity 2; an incumbent gets severity 1 when a substitute is cheaper all-in by 10 bps or more.
pillars.data_source: Web search; justETF profile pages (verified); issuer KIDs and notices
pillars.evidence: A fee rise is a structural trigger, and redirecting new money to a cheaper line costs nothing (Sharpe 1991).

pillars.name: Satellite thesis log (record only)
pillars.definition: Quarterly, for each held or policy satellite, the agent records cited structural facts that bear on 10-year cash flows or investability, with base rates, and a verdict (intact, weakened or broken). Weight 0: it never changes a score or freezes a sleeve. Facts on the fixed list (sanctions, capital controls, exchange closure, delisting) are passed to EVT07, which alone can gate.
pillars.data_source: Web search with at least 2 cited sources; central banks, regulators, statistics agencies
pillars.evidence: Auditors: a qualitative verdict moved money on judgement. News sentiment is priced within days (Tetlock 2007). The log lets REC03 test whether verdicts predict anything.

pillars.name: Index methodology, reclassification and mega-cap events
pillars.definition: Agent tracks benchmark switches, provider consultations, capping-rule changes, special rebalances, country reclassifications and single-company events that move top-10 weights. Weight 0 in X (not backtestable). Recorded; it feeds DUR08 and triggers an immediate recompute of FIT and CON from fresh holdings.
pillars.data_source: Web search; MSCI, FTSE Russell, S&P DJI and Nasdaq announcements; SEC EDGAR
pillars.evidence: Index rule changes shift the exposure before holdings files show it (Petajisto 2011).

pillars.name: Issuer, custodian and counterparty health
pillars.definition: Agent detects issuers exiting European ETFs, custodian or administrator changes (including ETC vault and custodian changes, which trigger a DUR02 re-check), lending or swap-counterparty incidents, and regulatory sanctions on an issuer or depositary. Applies to every line of that issuer. Penalty-only in the line score; severity 2 or more blocks deposits.
pillars.data_source: Web search; Central Bank of Ireland, CSSF and FCA notices; issuer releases
pillars.evidence: Issuer-level events hit every line at once and appear in fund data only late.

pillars.name: Tax and legal regime for the owner
pillars.data_source: Web search; IRS, Revenue.ie, UAE MoF, CRA
pillars.evidence: The Irish wrapper is worth 30-40 bps a year plus estate-tax protection (plan v5 P2), more than any tested edge.

pillars.name: Sanctions, capital controls and market access (gate)
pillars.definition: Agent detects sanctions, capital controls, exchange closures, investment bans and delisting risk affecting look-through holdings, estimates the affected weight per line, and proposes rows for config/restricted_markets.csv with a primary-source URL and quoted text, which code checks before CON04 uses them. Severity 3 freezes deposits to affected lines. Weight 0 in X.
pillars.data_source: Web search; OFAC, EU and UK sanctions lists; index-provider notices
pillars.evidence: Russia 2022 losses could not be traded around. The hazard is now counted once, as a gate.

pillars.name: Broker, venue and funding channel
pillars.definition: Agent watches IBKR changes for UAE clients (US$1.70 minimum, FX terms and US$2 minimum, product access, KID), fractional LSE ETF shares, LSE outages, the CBUAE peg stance and UAE remittance fees. Weight 0. Confirmed changes update the allocator constants and the funding block.
pillars.data_source: Web search; IBKR pricing and notices; LSE notices; CBUAE releases
pillars.evidence: The ticket and FX minimums and whole-share buying drive the monthly split and line choice. Fractional shares would reopen CSPX and CNDX.

pillars.name: Deposit-week calendar and market dislocations
pillars.definition: Agent lists deposit-week events (FOMC, US CPI and payrolls, ECB, BoE and BoJ, index rebalance days, US and UK holidays) and any ETF dislocation or LSE outage, and recommends the order day and hour. It may delay an order by at most 1 week and never skips a deposit or triggers a sale. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: Web search; central-bank, index-provider and exchange calendars
pillars.evidence: Spreads widen around releases and rebalances (Petajisto 2011, 2017). Pausing in a crisis has cost more than the crisis (S8).

pillars.name: CMA and valuation data harvest (code-checked)
pillars.definition: Each quarter the agent extracts numbers only, from CMA releases and regional CAPE readings. Each row is written to config/cma.csv or config/cape.csv with a URL, the quoted text span and a date. Code fetches the page and confirms the number appears in the span; failing rows are marked unverified and never read by any pillar. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: Web search; house PDFs; StarCapital and Research Affiliates pages
pillars.evidence: Auditors: hand-entered numbers flowed straight into EXR and FIT04 with no check. Only record-only pillars (EXR01, EXR05) read these files now.

allocation_method:
Three layers: the pool and its limits are policy, targets come from the owner now (and from scores only after REC04 passes), and routing happens monthly. The weekly run never moves money.

1. THE POOL. Sleeve lines are verified on yfinance as USD LSE lines on 2026-11-07. The universe file is to be updated before launch: add EXUS, ACWD and SPYY, remove EQAC, remove the duplicate CUSS, R2US, WSML and XDEW rows, and fix the VWRA TER to 0.14.
- Core, world: VWRA (designated). Chain FWRA, then ACWD (US$314.84); SPYY is listed but thin. At least 80% of the portfolio while REC04 fails.
- S&P 500: SPXS (US$14.95), VUAA (US$143.90), CSPX (US$802). Band 0-15%.
- Nasdaq-100: XNAS (US$63.16), CNDX (US$1,563), EQQU (US$665, distributing). Band 0-10%.
- Developed ex-US: EXUS (Xtrackers MSCI World ex USA 1C, US$44.75, listed 2024-03). Band 0-15%.
- Emerging markets: EIMI. Band 0-10%.
- Factor and small-cap: IWVL, IWQU, WSML. Band 0-10%.
- Gold: IGLN, via ELG01(b) and DUR02 (SGLD only after Invesco data is verified). 0 or 5%.
- Diversifier bonds: AGGU or 5+ year government bonds. Share D set by the owner at 0-20%, default 0, never moved by scores.
- Limits: any satellite is 0% or at least 5%. At most 4 lines in total (FIT11). Satellites total at most 20% of the portfolio. Satellites receive at most satellite_share (0 to 0.20) of the dollars deposited over any rolling 12 months; this keeps the DECISION_RULES 20% deposit cap and still allows one order a month.

2. TARGETS.
(a) Before REC04 passes (now). X is computed, logged and reported but sets no targets. Targets come only from config/portfolio.yaml policy_targets, set by the owner, for example {SP500: 0.10, NDX: 0.05}. Every policy must pass:
- the hard constraints: US no more than world +10 (FIT07), IT plus Communication no more than world +10 (FIT08), single name 7% or less (FIT09), tracking error 3% or less (FIT10), drawdown budget world +5 (RSK06), and risk-contribution ratio 1.5 or less (RSK07);
- the REC07 test, re-run whenever the policy changes. The owner note labels the policy 'owner policy, not evidence-favoured', and also 'regime bet' if it lost in any REC07 period.
With satellite_share = 0 or no policy_targets, every deposit goes to the core (DECISION_RULES rule 2 default).
(b) After REC04 passes. The owner may set target_mode: score.
- X is the 13-week mean on the sleeve's reference index (never the best line).
- A sleeve qualifies when X is 55 or more at two consecutive live quarterly reviews (no backfilled quarters) and FIT04 alpha is above 0 at the proposed weight.
- Target = band max x clip((X - 55) / 15, 0, 1), rounded to 0 or at least 5%, then scaled down until every constraint holds.
- Hysteresis: a change of at least 2.5 points and at most 5 points per sleeve per quarter. The owner confirms each change.
- The 20% portfolio and rolling-12 deposit limits still apply. Going higher needs an owner CHANGELOG entry plus 36 months of REC03 live record.

3. MONTHLY DEPOSIT.
(a) Funding. The owner records in config/portfolio.yaml how the AED reaches IBKR: method, bank fee, correspondent fee, FX minimum and checked_on. Let F be the fixed USD cost per conversion. Convert every k months, where k in {1, 2, 3} minimises F/k + ((k-1)/2) x 680.74 x 0.4%. With only the US$2 FX minimum, k = 1; with F = US$10, k = 3. This month: 2,500 / 3.6725 = US$680.74, minus US$2 = US$678.74. C = that plus any residue (at most one month's deposit).
(b) Gaps. Gap g = target x (portfolio value + C) - sleeve value (FIT01). If positions are missing or stale, or no gap exceeds US$100, everything goes to the core.
(c) Routing. All of C goes in one order to the largest positive gap. A satellite may receive it only if the rolling-12-month satellite share of deposits stays at or below satellite_share; otherwise the core gets it. A second order to the next gap is placed only if both orders are at least US$340. Never more than 2 orders a month.
(d) Line choice. The line must pass:
- ELG01-ELG05, ELG08, ELG09 and FIT11;
- CON04 at 5% or less, and no EVT01, EVT02 or EVT05 event at severity 2 or more, and no EVT07 event at severity 3;
- a line score of 40 or more.
Among those, buy the lowest CST10. The new-money line changes only when a challenger is at least 5 bps a year cheaper at 2 consecutive monthly runs; the old line is kept, not sold.
(e) Whole shares: buy floor((order - 1.70) / price). If the cheapest line does not fit the order, use the next line within 10 bps a year all-in; otherwise route to the next gap.
(f) Fallback. If no line in the target sleeve passes, go to the next sleeve. If none passes, buy the core chain (VWRA, then FWRA, then ACWD), requiring only ELG01, ELG02, ELG05 and EVT01 below severity 2. Cash is never held for more than one month.
(g) Execution. Place the order on the EVT09 day, as a limit at mid plus half the spread, 14:30-16:15 London for US-heavy sleeves (MAC03 stress: a limit at mid). Log the fill for CST09, REC05 and REC06.
(h) In a drawdown nothing changes: new money fills whatever fell.

Worked example (illustrative). The owner holds VWRA US$20,000 and sets policy_targets S&P 500 10%, satellite_share 0.20. The previous 12 deposits all went to the core. C = US$678.74, so the portfolio after the deposit is US$20,678.74.
- Gaps: S&P 500 +US$2,067.87; core (90%) -US$1,389.13.
- Rolling-12 satellite share after this order is 678.74 / (12 x 678.74) = 8.3%, within 20%. Route to the S&P 500 sleeve.
- Line, by CST10: SPXS about -26.5 bps (3-year gap +19.3 bps over CSPX, minus the half TAX03 haircut of 9.7) against VUAA about -17 bps. SPXS is cheaper by about 9.5 bps, so it is chosen once it has led at 2 monthly runs.
- Order: 45 SPXS at US$14.95 = US$672.75 plus US$1.70 commission; residue US$4.29.
- Next month the S&P 500 sleeve can take a second deposit (16.7%). A third within 12 months would exceed 20%, so it goes to the core. The S&P 500 sleeve therefore gets at most 2 of every 12 deposits until it reaches 10%.

4. WEEKLY. All 318 unique lines are scored. The report shows three separate rankings and never one composite:
(i) line scores ranked within each sleeve;
(ii) exposure score X by sleeve against VWRA = 50, with its trend;
(iii) the fit view of each sleeve's best line against the current portfolio.
It also shows each holding against VWRA (MOM05), gates, events, coverage, missing pillars and the drawdown state.

5. RECORDS. REC02 logs every month. REC04 decides whether X may set targets. REC07 re-tests the owner's policy. Changes to DECISION_RULES rule 2 go through CHANGELOG: satellite_share now caps the rolling-12-month share of deposited dollars, and its destination is the policy-target gap rather than the top-ranked ETF.
